detail.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.summary: Memory reliability and retention time are fundamentally limited by energy dissipation. Our revision incorporates findings that non-equilibrium environments and non-reciprocal couplings modulate Landauer erasure costs, establishing that predictive power in information engines is constrained by available energy and coarse-grained state access. Additionally, we contextualize these physical costs with operational overheads, where excessive data retention in cloud systems demonstrates a practical parallel to thermodynamic inefficiency, albeit driven by configuration rather than entropy bounds.
detail.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate specific recent findings on non-reciprocal information engines and practical operational costs, fulfilling the project requirements.

detail.title: Synthesis of Operational Memory Foundations
detail.summary: This cycle completes the systematic revision of three core notebooks focusing on the thermodynamic and operational costs of memory. We integrate findings on coarse-graining, non-equilibrium driven dynamics, and passive degree-of-freedom coupling. Key insights identify that persistent physical states only function as effective memory when they demonstrably reduce future uncertainty or dissipation, a condition constrained by the resolution of the observer's model.
